records.reason: New m30 at 5/1 establishes a moderate-ratio anchor for para-bromoacetophenone. Related measured fluorinated and ortho-brominated ketones provide structural references, but their response need not transfer to this substitution pattern.

Pair m30 at 50/1 with its selected 5/1 condition, holding loading settings fixed. The predicted change from 6.42/13.30 to 16.77/35.56 mL tests transfer of solvent-response slope to an unseen aryl ketone.

New m35 at 5/1 anchors para-iodoacetophenone alongside the m30 pair. Its predicted finish differs from m30 despite identical donor/acceptor counts, testing structural information beyond a generic halogenated-ketone category.

The matched m35 50/1 point tests its predicted 10.30/28.47 mL response under weaker elution. Together with m35 at 5/1, it distinguishes a scaffold-specific slope from a correction transferred indiscriminately from measured ketones.

New m180 at 5/1 explores a fused cyclic ketone close to observed m179 and m182. Their different measured profiles motivate direct calibration of ring environment rather than assuming that all fused monoketones behave alike.

Complete the fixed-loading m180 strength contrast at 50/1. Its predicted 24.16/49.44 mL endpoints remain untested; the pair determines whether the model correctly locates substantial retention growth in this unseen cyclic scaffold.

At m125 0/1 and 100-ul sample volume, the 500-ul DCM loading plug contrasts with measured 300-ul settings. Test whether the plug-volume difference observed at 50-ul sample volume persists at a second loading.

Fill m125's missing 100-ul sample point at 1/1 with 300 ul DCM. Measured 50- and 150-ul samples bracket this condition, allowing the local endpoint response to be assessed without changing loading-solvent volume.

Measure the middle loading at m81 10/1. Measured V2 differed from 17.39 mL at 50 ul to 9.74 mL at 150 ul, whereas current predictions are almost loading-invariant. This tests the contrast without presuming a linear causal mass effect.

Add m81 at 20/1 with the same 100-ul sample volume as its selected 10/1 point. Determine whether finish remains modest as EA decreases or expands again, following the recently measured compact high-loading result.

Test whether m197's long finish at 2/1 persists at 100-ul sample volume. The measured 150-ul sample finished at 26.95 mL; the current prediction here is already 25.34 mL, so this evaluates transfer of newly learned behavior.

At m197 150 ul, compare 5/1 directly with the measured 2/1 condition. Predicted V2 is 21.87 mL, below the measured 26.95 mL at 2/1 despite weaker elution. Determine whether that contraction is real or misplaced model curvature.

Fill m92's 100-ul loading at 5/1 with its EA loading plug unchanged. Measured 50- and 150-ul samples differ substantially; the middle label can constrain the conditional loading response and separate onset displacement from finish changes.
Measure m92 at 2/1 and 150 ul to ask whether the high-loading displacement recently observed at 20/1 also occurs with more EA. Existing 100-ul measurements at 2/1 provide a local loading reference.

Locate m182's finish between measured 0/1 and 10/1 conditions at fixed 50-ul loading. Recent feedback revealed a substantial finish underestimate at 0/1; this intermediate condition directly calibrates V2 growth within that gap.

Extend sparsely sampled bromo-salicylaldehyde m190 from its measured 1/1 anchor to 20/1. Heterogeneous phenolic-aldehyde outcomes motivate this transfer test without imposing one universal OH or intramolecular-hydrogen-bond correction.

Probe cyclopropyl beta-ketoester m94 at 5/1, predicted at 11.46/29.55 mL. Its measured anchor is at 0/1; recent compact m81 feedback cautions against inferring finish solely from carbonyl or acceptor counts.

Pair m94 at 20/1 with its selected 5/1 row at identical loading settings. Predicted endpoints of 23.92/41.01 mL test its local slope against the heterogeneous responses already measured in related beta-ketoesters.
Measure m82 at 10/1 beyond its existing 2/1 observations. This tests the predicted rise to a 34.34-mL finish and connects a sparsely anchored ethyl beta-ketoester to better sampled carbonyl families.

Fill the m95 10/1 gap between moderate-ratio observations and its measured late 20/1 regime. Alongside selected m82, it tests family transfer while retaining differences in mass and DCM loading volume as possible contributors.

The m11 2/1 prediction finishes at 23.64 mL, above the measured 15.70 mL at 5/1 under matched loading settings. Measure this missing point to distinguish a genuine local minimum from misplaced response curvature.

First of a fixed-50-ul m191 pair testing a predicted V2 contraction from 40.47 mL at 1/1 to 26.60 mL at 2/1. The measured later 10/1 condition finishes at 57.76 mL, making the unanchored early curve informative.

Complete the m191 1/1-to-2/1 contrast with sample volume and 400-ul DCM plug held fixed. Two labels determine whether the predicted finish contraction survives measurement and clarify the early response of this dialdehyde.

Bridge m128's moderate-ratio anchors and its measured late 20/1 behavior. At 10/1 and 100-ul sample volume, predicted endpoints of 20.69/40.35 mL test where the sulfur-containing ketone enters its steep response regime.

Establish an EA-rich baseline for m129, currently represented by a measured 50/1 condition. Its predicted 9.91/21.48 mL endpoints could reflect genuine sulfide-aldehyde retention or transfer from other sulfur scaffolds.

Pair m129 at 5/1 with its selected 0/1 baseline at fixed 100-ul sample and 300-ul DCM plug. This supplies an early response slope before its measured 50/1 regime and tests transfer from the sulfide-ketone family.

Measure sulfoxide m199 at 5/1, predicted at 10.26/23.01 mL. Existing lower-ratio labels allow a test of finish plateau versus continued growth and help distinguish sulfoxide behavior from the selected aryl sulfides.

Extend nitrophenethyl alcohol m200 to 2/1 at 100 ul. A measured 1/1, 50-ul sample already finished at 37.40 mL; this condition tests the combined nitro/alcohol environment in the predicted 45.60-mL finish regime.

Anchor m205 at 1/1 and 150 ul before its measured very late 5/1 regime. Together with the selected 2/1 condition, this tests the beginning of a steep alcohol response at fully matched loading settings.

Complete the m205 1/1-to-2/1 pair at 150 ul and 400 ul DCM. Determine whether its measured late 5/1 behavior is preceded by the predicted 17.43/34.41 mL intermediate response, calibrating onset and finish separately.

The current m71 1/1 onset prediction is only 0.93 mL, an unanchored dip between otherwise compact measured profiles. This targeted control tests an unusual onset prediction in a very lipophilic thiophene.

Pentafluorobenzene m156 at 2/1 and 50 ul tests a predicted compact 6.44/9.25 mL regime before its measured weaker-eluent finish expansion. This ordinary structural control helps locate where finish growth begins.

hypotheses.content: Increasing PE/EA normally weakens normal-phase elution by reducing EA, but the magnitude, transition location, and coupling of V1 and V2 remain scaffold-specific. Predicted local contractions require measurement rather than automatic acceptance or forced monotonic correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched ratio contrasts can teach local response curvature and endpoint coupling instead of propagating one solvent correction across unrelated rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the predicted contractions in m191, m197, and m11 survive measurement, and where does the steep m205 response begin at fixed loading?

hypotheses.content: Recorded loading settings may affect onset and finish differently, while current predictions are often nearly loading-invariant. Repeated-tuple scatter also exists, so apparent loading effects should be treated as conditional relationships rather than established causal mass laws.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Missing middle loadings and matched plug-volume contrasts can constrain conditional responses and reveal where loading features are useful. They cannot resolve unrecorded causes of variability.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m125's plug-volume differences transfer to 100-ul samples, and do m81, m92, and m197 show coherent loading responses at fixed ratios?

hypotheses.content: Substantial V2 errors can occur with comparatively accurate V1, and neither a broad predicted elution interval nor a large single-model quantile width reliably identifies their direction. Finish behavior needs direct calibration across compact and broad regimes.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Endpoint-specific labels can repair finish predictions without unnecessarily shifting onset or inflating every carbonyl-containing compound's interval.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m81 remain compact at 20/1, and can an intermediate m182 label locate finish growth after its recently observed early tail?

hypotheses.content: Local structural environment is likely necessary for transferring retention response among donor-free aryl ketones, fused ketones, and beta-ketoesters. Predictions for unseen m30, m35, and m180 and sparsely anchored m94 remain untested; donor-containing multifunctional scaffolds also need local anchors.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Within-molecule ratio pairs on new or sparsely sampled structures provide graph-level training signals that distinguish local carbonyl and heteroatom environments beyond descriptor counts.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which predicted slopes transfer to the new ketones and m94, and which require scaffold-specific corrections after recorded loading features are considered?

hypotheses.content: Low-polarity and acceptor-free compounds contain both compact regimes and condition-dependent finish expansion. Targeted ordinary labels are useful where the model predicts unusual onset dips or an unanchored transition.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These controls constrain ordinary-regime onset and finish while testing specific model behavior, limiting spillover from corrections learned on strongly retained compounds.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Is m71's predicted 1/1 onset dip real, and does m156 remain compact at 2/1 before its known weaker-eluent finish expansion?

hypotheses.content: Aryl methyl sulfides and sulfoxides may have distinct baseline retention and solvent-response curves that TPSA or acceptor counts inadequately summarize. The low-ratio response of m129 and the post-2/1 response of m199 are particularly weakly anchored.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Labels spanning sulfide ketone, sulfide aldehyde, and sulfoxide environments can improve structural transfer while separating baseline shifts from ratio-dependent growth.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m129 already retain substantially at 0/1, how much does it change by 5/1, and does m199 plateau or continue growing after 2/1?

feedback_interpretation: Recent outcomes favor selective finish repair rather than a broad late-retention correction. At fixed 150-ul sample and 200-ul DCM plug, m72 increased from 8.18/25.80 mL at 2/1 to 13.07/35.59 mL at 5/1, supporting a local ratio response. Historical acquisition-time V2 errors were -12.16 mL for m197 and -7.48 mL for m182 despite relatively small onset errors, whereas m81's finish was overpredicted by 7.20 mL. Several ordinary controls were accurate or had modest finish overprediction. The m125 outcome strengthens the case for a loading-plug-volume contrast, while m92's high-loading 20/1 outcome motivates a strength-dependent loading test. These are historical acquisition errors, not current-model residuals; some current predictions already incorporate the new behavior. Repeated measurements at identical recorded settings also temper causal interpretations of loading differences. Earlier solvent terminology needs correction: increasing PE/EA reduces EA and normally weakens normal-phase elution. DCM, PE, and EA in the loading-solvent field describe the loading plug.
batch_rationale: The 32 distinct selections link local failure repair to structural transfer. Missing loading points for m125, m81, m92, and m197 test relationships that current predictions represent almost flatly. Matched ratio pairs for m191 and m205 distinguish predicted curvature from measured response, while m197 and m11 challenge specific predicted contractions. New-scaffold pairs for m30, m35, and m180 and the m94 pair supply within-molecule slopes, making their labels informative beyond isolated novelty. Additional beta-ketoester, phenolic-aldehyde, nitro-alcohol, and sulfur probes address sparsely anchored environments connected to observed successes and failures. The m71 and m156 controls target concrete ordinary-regime questions. Cross-molecule comparisons retain density, loading amount, and plug-volume differences as possible contributors rather than attributing differences solely to substituents. Quantile widths and CW distances are secondary diagnostics, particularly given frequent zero V2 lower quantiles and quantile crossings. The intended benefit is improved conditional V1/V2 prediction across the Row-distribution through transferable structural signals, local response slopes, and endpoint-specific calibration.
